editorial:
Imagine a doctor who decides that the kindest thing he can do for his patients is to help them die. That is exactly what you get with this movie. It follows Dr. Jack Kevorkian, a man who becomes famous and hated for helping people with terrible diseases end their pain. The vibe is a mix of a courtroom drama and a personal character study. You will see Jack as a grumpy but determined man who truly believes he is doing the right thing, even when the whole world tells him he is a criminal. It is a heavy topic, but the movie keeps things moving by showing the clashes between Jack and the law.

What really makes this work is the acting. The lead actor does a great job showing Jack's stubborn side and his weird sense of humor. The pacing is solid, though some of the legal talk can feel a bit long. If you like stories about people who challenge the system, you will love this. Since it is an older TV movie, you might want to hunt for a high-quality digital version. It is definitely a conversation starter for a movie night with friends.
endingExplained: The movie ends with Jack finally facing the music in court. After years of fighting, he is convicted of second-degree murder and sent to prison. However, the film shows that while he lost his freedom, he won the debate. He managed to bring the conversation about the right to die into the open for everyone to discuss. He accepts his jail time as the price for changing how people think about death.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about rebels and legal battles.
